sentences.text: Heard Sri Anish Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Narendra Kumar, learned counsel for the informant as well as Ms. Ifra Islam, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

2. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 467 of 2023, U/S 376, 384, 506 IPC, 3/4 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station Loni Border, District Ghaziabad, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have befriended the informant on social media,
whereafter, he called her to his room and forcibly entered into corporeal relationship with her and had video graphed the said act.

The applicant is stated to have, subsequently, called her on 7.8.2023 Vivek vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86535051/
1 to a guest house, whereat her entry was made on the basis of fake documents in the name of one Deepika, and thereupon had taken her to a room and had again committed the said offence and had video graphed it.

entities.text: 7.8.2023 Vivek vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is stated to have even demanded Rs. 20,000/- from her lest he shall make the said video graphs of the victim viral.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
It is stated that he has nothing to do with the said offence.
It is stated that the FIR is delayed by about one and a half months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

5. It is stated that the victim is the consenting party, as is but evident from the fact that she had come thrice to meet the applicant to Ghaziabad and the last incident is stated to have occurred on 7.8.2023.
Learned counsel has stated that the age of the victim is stated to be 15 years, which is false.

As per her school certificate, the date of birth is stated to be 7.7.2008.
6.

Learned counsel has stated that the victim may be considered major in light of the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673, wherein it has been stated that it is more often in the Indian Society that person shows the age of their wards much below than their actual age.

entities.text: Sushil Kumar vs. Rakesh Kumar, (2003) 8 SCC 673
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case of Brij Mohan Singh vs. Priya Brat Narain Sinha, AIR 1965 SC 282, this Court, inter alia, observed that in actual life it often happens that persons give false age of the boy at the time of his admission to a school so that later in life he would have an advantage when seeking public service for which a minimum age for eligibility is often prescribed.

entities.text: Brij Mohan Singh vs. Priya Brat Narain Sinha, AIR 1965 SC 282
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further stated that there is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 23.9.2023.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

8. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the victim is minor, coupled by the fact that she has been forcibly subjected to sexual assault by the victim.
9. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

A person's right to life and liberty,
guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because he or she is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.

2 10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA for the State.

11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record regarding complicity of the accused, the inordinate delay in lodging of the FIR, larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

12. Let the applicant- Vivek, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
13. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

14. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
